final.research_question: Does changing the offensive five (lineup) itself influence the shot mix of a team?
final.evidence_use: The absence of prior internal project research on this specific question means this is a novel inquiry within the project's history. My assessment of testability and risks is based on the available data and general methodological considerations rather than prior findings or failures. This necessitates a comprehensive design that addresses potential confounding factors from first principles.

prior_work.summary: No prior internal project research was found on this specific question. This study would be a new investigation into the phenomenon.

risks.text: Shot mix is influenced by numerous factors beyond personnel, including opponent defensive scheme, game state (score, time), coaching instructions, and even individual player hot/cold streaks. Robust controls are critical to isolate the effect of the offensive lineup itself.

Many unique five-player lineups may have very limited playing time together, especially across multiple seasons. This sparsity will make it difficult to estimate reliable shot mix distributions for specific, rarely used lineups, potentially limiting the scope of analysis to more common lineup combinations or aggregate effects.

While the overall dataset is large, the number of distinct lineup changes and the number of possessions played by each lineup before another change might be insufficient to detect subtle but real changes in shot mix with adequate statistical power, especially after applying stringent controls and considering multiplicity.

design.estimand: The causal effect of a change in offensive five-player lineup on the team's subsequent shot mix, specifically the distribution of shot attempts by zone (e.g., restricted area, paint non-restricted, mid-range, 3-point zones) and shot type (e.g., catch-and-shoot, pull-up, post-up, drive-and-kick).
design.unit: Offensive possessions. A 'change' event will be defined as a substitution that alters at least one player in the offensive five. We will analyze segments of possessions following these changes.
design.sample: All offensive possessions from NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs. To ensure robust estimates, only lineup segments with a minimum threshold of possessions (e.g., 5 or more) will be included for analysis of shot mix within that segment.
design.power: Power calculations will be performed to determine the minimum detectable effect size for common lineup changes (e.g., changes occurring in >100 game segments across the dataset). The goal is to achieve 80% power at alpha=0.05 for detecting a 2-3 percentage point shift in the proportion of shots from a major zone for these common cases.
design.controls: A mixed-effects regression model will be used, including fixed effects for game, team, and potentially individual players to control for baseline tendencies. Key control variables will include game state (score differential, time remaining in quarter/game), opponent defensive scheme (derived from play-by-play data, e.g., indicators for zone defense, specific pick-and-roll coverages if discernible), and prior offensive pace. A difference-in-differences approach comparing shot mix in possessions immediately before and after a lineup change within the same game and against the same opponent will be explored to mitigate confounding.
design.falsification: A placebo test will examine whether similar shifts in shot mix occur in periods without any offensive personnel change, but where other control variables (game state, opponent defense) fluctuate. Another falsification test could involve examining effects on defensive shot mix, which should not be directly influenced by offensive personnel changes.
design.multiplicity: Given that multiple shot zones and shot types will be analyzed, adjustments for multiple comparisons will be applied. This could involve False Discovery Rate (FDR) control or Bonferroni correction, depending on the number of hypotheses tested and the desired balance between Type I and Type II errors.
design.decision_rule: The hypothesis will be supported if statistically significant shifts in shot mix (p < 0.05 after multiplicity adjustment) are observed following offensive lineup changes, after robustly controlling for confounding factors, and the observed effect sizes are considered practically meaningful (e.g., a change of at least 2 percentage points in a major shot zone or type category).
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 regular season and playoffs per-game files from the NBA stats API (play-by-play, substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary) and derived play-type possession records.
